extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners and parties in PTAB inter partes review proceedings (petitioners, patent owners, PTAB judges), and USPTO examiners and attorneys
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and orders from the Director of the USPTO addressing when Director Review is appropriate where the Board denied institution under 35 U.S.C. § 325(d), including how to evaluate whether the examiner committed an apparent/material error (with emphasis on relying on prior IPR findings about the same prior art) and remand instructions to the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of arguments showing examiner error under Ecto World
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioner must sufficiently argue examiner error under Ecto World (IPR2024-01280, Paper 13) — i.e., explain how the examiner 'erred by misapprehending or overlooking' the cited prior art (here, Nishida).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director found Petitioner 'sufficiently argued under Ecto World how the examiner erred in overlooking the prior art.' Petitioner should point to specific examiner misapprehensions or oversights and explain how those errors affected patentability, citing record evidence and prior IPR findings when relevant (see Paper 16, 4; Ecto World, Paper 13 at 5–6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Apparent material error by the Office standard
rubrics_metrics.description: To overcome a §325(d) denial, a petitioner may demonstrate an 'apparent error in the examiner’s findings' that is 'material to the patentability of the challenged claims.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director relied on prior Board findings (e.g., that Nishida discloses 'simultaneously knitting a textile element with a surrounding textile structure') to conclude the examiner’s error was apparent and material. Showing prior authoritative findings that the same reference discloses claim limitations supports a conclusion of material examiner error (citing IPR2016-00922, Ex. 1017, 25–26; IPR2024-00460, Ex. 1069, 23–24; and IPR2024-00460 Paper 30 at 29–30).

rubrics_metrics.name: Weight of prior IPR findings and consistency across proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Board and Director should consider factual findings from prior IPRs involving the same patent and the same prior art; prior determinations that a reference discloses a limitation bear on whether the examiner erred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioner may and should cite prior IPR institution or final written decisions that found the same teachings (here Nishida) disclose the limitations at issue. The Director noted that prior Board findings that Nishida discloses 'simultaneously knitting' strengthen the petitioner's showing and that the Board erred by not adequately considering those prior findings when denying institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitioner’s burden to carry under the Board’s §325(d) framework
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner bears the burden to carry its arguments under the Board’s §325(d) framework — demonstrating examiner error and materiality sufficient to overcome denial of institution based on prior art previously considered by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arguments should (1) identify the particular error (misapprehension/overlook), (2) tie that error to claim limitations and patentability, and (3) use supporting evidence such as prior IPR findings or petition exhibits. Failure to meet this burden supports denial (the Decision initially found Petitioner failed to carry this burden, but Director disagreed as to Nishida).

rubrics_metrics.name: Persuasiveness of additional prior art grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Separate grounds relying on other references (e.g., Günther, Orei) must be persuasive on their own merits; unpersuasive arguments will not justify institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director expressly found Petitioner’s additional arguments as to Günther and Orei 'unpersuasive' (DR Request 5–9, 12–15), indicating that mere citation of references without adequate explanatory linkage to claim limitations and materiality will fail. Present clear claim-charting, reasoning, and evidence for each reference relied upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remand and procedural timeline requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: When Director Review is granted and the Decision denying institution is vacated, the case is remanded to the Board with instructions to consider the specified grounds (here, Nishida) and determine whether to institute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order: 'Director Review is granted; the Decision denying institution ... is vacated; and the case is remanded to the Board for further proceedings consistent with this Order.' Absent good cause, the Board 'shall issue its decision within 30 days of this Order.'
